questions.text: Injury to which cranial nerve leads to loss of the efferent limb of the pupillary light reflex?
questions.explanation: The optic nerve (CN II) is the afferent limb. The oculomotor nerve (CN III) carries parasympathetic fibers that constrict the pupil, serving as the efferent limb.
questions.keyConcept: CN II is afferent; CN III is efferent in pupillary light reflex.

questions.text: Which layer of the retina contains the cell bodies of the photoreceptor cells (rods and cones)?
questions.explanation: The outer nuclear layer of the retina contains the nuclei/cell bodies of photoreceptors (rods and cones).
questions.keyConcept: Outer nuclear layer contains rod and cone nuclei.

chapters.title: Biochemistry
chapters.subtitle: Visual Cycle and Vitamin A metabolism

questions.text: Which derivative of Vitamin A binds with opsin to form rhodopsin in rod cells?
questions.explanation: 11-cis-retinal is the light-sensitive chromophore that binds to opsin to synthesize rhodopsin.
questions.keyConcept: 11-cis-retinal is the active Vitamin A derivative in vision transduction.

questions.text: Describe the physiological process of accommodation when looking at a near object.
questions.explanation: Accommodation involves ciliary muscle contraction, zonular fibers relaxation, and lens rounding.
questions.keyConcept: Parasympathetic stimulation increases refractive power of the lens.
questions.modelAnswer:
Accommodation process for near vision:
1. Ciliary muscle contraction: Triggered by parasympathetic fibers from Edinger-Westphal nucleus (CN III).
2. Zonular fibers (suspensory ligaments) relax.
3. The elastic lens capsules rounds/bulges, increasing its anterior curvature and refractive power.
4. Pupil constriction (iris closes to increase depth of focus).
5. Convergence of both eyes (medial recti contract).

questions.text: Which serovars of Chlamydia trachomatis are the primary cause of Trachoma, the leading infectious cause of blindness worldwide?
questions.explanation: Serovars A, B, Ba, and C cause Trachoma. Serovars D-K cause neonatal conjunctivitis and genitourinary infections. Serovars L1-L3 cause LGV.
options: Serovars A, B, Ba, and C

chapters.title: Pathology
chapters.subtitle: Pathology of Eye and Ear diseases

questions.text: Which ocular condition is characterized histologically by progressive degeneration and loss of retinal ganglion cell axons, accompanied by cup-to-disc ratio expansion?
questions.explanation: Glaucoma is characterized by retinal ganglion cell death and optic nerve head cupping, often associated with elevated intraocular pressure.
questions.keyConcept: Glaucoma results in optic neuropathy with characteristic cupping.

chapters.title: Pharmacology
chapters.subtitle: Drug therapy of glaucoma and eye conditions

questions.text: Which class of topical glaucoma medications lowers intraocular pressure primarily by increasing uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humor?
questions.explanation: Prostaglandin analogs (e.g. Latanoprost) act by increasing uveoscleral outflow. Beta-blockers and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors decrease aqueous humor production.

chapters.title: Ophthalmology

questions.text: Explain the significance of finding an Afferent Pupillary Defect (Marcus Gunn Pupil) during an examination.
questions.explanation: A Marcus Gunn pupil signifies unilateral optic nerve pathology or severe retinal disease.
questions.keyConcept: Afferent defects show paradoxically dilated pupils on direct illumination during swinging flashlight test.
questions.modelAnswer:
Significance of Marcus Gunn Pupil (APD):
- Indicated by: Paradoxical dilation of the affected pupil when light is swung from the normal eye to the affected eye during the swinging flashlight test.
- Clinical cause: Suggests significant damage to the afferent visual pathway (most commonly optic neuritis, optic nerve compression, or severe ischemic retinal damage) anterior to the optic chiasm.

chapters.title: E.N.T.
chapters.subtitle: Otology, Rhinology, Hearing loss and sensory nerve disorders

questions.text: Compare between Conductive hearing loss and Sensorineural hearing loss in terms of Rinne and Weber test results.
questions.explanation: Rinne test is negative in conductive loss. Weber lateralizes to the diseased side in conductive and normal side in sensorineural.
questions.keyConcept: Tuning fork tests distinguish conductive from sensorineural deficits.
questions.modelAnswer:
| Test | Conductive Hearing Loss (Left Ear) | Sensorineural Hearing Loss (Left Ear) |
|---|---|---|
| Rinne Test (Left Ear) | Negative (Bone Conduction > Air Conduction) | Positive (Air Conduction > Bone Conduction) |
| Weber Test | Lateralizes to the Left (affected) ear | Lateralizes to the Right (normal/better) ear |
| Common causes | Otitis media, wax accumulation, otosclerosis | Presbycusis, noise exposure, acoustic neuroma |
